source_caption:
John Carpenter’s They Live is a sci-fi satire about a drifter named Nada who discovers that a group of aliens is secretly controlling society. After finding a pair of special sunglasses, he can suddenly see the subliminal messages hidden in advertisements, magazines, and everyday life, including commands like “OBEY” and “CONSUME.”

Beneath its sci-fi premise, the film is a sharp critique of consumerism, corporate power, class inequality, and the way people can be influenced without realizing it. Carpenter based the film on the 1963 short story “Eight O’Clock in the Morning” by Ray Nelson, and the sunglasses became one of the movie’s most memorable metaphors for becoming aware of what is happening beneath the surface. Starring Roddy Piper and Keith David, They Live has since become one of Carpenter’s most enduring cult films.

source_details.synopsis: They Live is a 1988 American science fiction action horror film written, directed, and scored by John Carpenter, and starring Roddy Piper, Keith David, and Meg Foster. It was based on the 1963 short story "Eight O'Clock in the Morning" by Ray Nelson. Set in Los Angeles, it follows a working class drifter (Piper) who discovers that the ruling class are camouflaged aliens, which drives him on a quest to expose them to the world. Having acquired the film rights to the story prior to the production of They Live, Carpenter used the story as the basis for the screenplay's structure, which he wrote under the pseudonym "Frank Armitage."
